shortDescription: Brazil's federal tax revenue rose 8.25% in real terms in August from a year earlier, totaling 235.57 billion reais ($45.95 billion), official data showed on Tuesday.($1 = 5.1267 reais)

children: Brazil's federal tax revenue rose 8.25% in real terms in August from a year earlier, totaling 235.57 billion reais ($45.95 billion), official data showed on Tuesday.
The result was the highest ever recorded for August in the tax revenue service's series, which dates back to 1995.
The performance mirrors record highs posted in every month so far this year.
Year-to-date revenue rose a real 7.12%, also a record for the series.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's government has largely relied on stronger revenue collection to improve fiscal accounts and pursue a narrower budget gap.
Still, an effective primary deficit is expected this year when all public expenditures are taken into account.
The tax revenue service said higher corporate profit-related tax collection was among the main drivers of August's result.
It also highlighted stronger social security contributions, reflecting real wage bill growth and the gradual rollback of payroll tax breaks under the Lula administration.
Revenue from capital income posted robust growth, the agency said, citing stronger collection from fixed-income investments and dividends.
Gains from dividends were exempt until last year.
